full_judgment:
3. Dr M Zahir, the learned Counsel for the petitioners, submits that the suit having been filed detailing the elements of fraud committed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, unless there is an order of attachment before judgment, by practicing fraud the foreign perpetrators would take away the proceeds of the letter of credit from Bangladesh. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the letter of credit money already belonged to the defendants, which money should not leave the jurisdiction of the Court whereby any possible decree would be frustrated and, as such, there ought to have been an order of attachment before judgment. 

 5. (1) Where, at any stage of a suit, the Court is satisfied by affidavit or otherwise, that the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that may be passed against him,- 

 (b) is about to remove the whole or any part of his property from, the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court the Court may direct the defendant, within a time to be fixed by it, either to furnish security, in such sum as may be specified in the order, to produce and place at the disposal of the Court, when required, the said property or the value of the same, or such portion thereof as may be sufficient to satisfy the decree, or to appear and show cause why he should not furnish security. 

 6. This section is designed to prevent a decree that may be passed from being infructuous. On an application under Order XXXVIII rule 5 the Court may direct the defendant within a time fixed by it either to furnish the security as may be specified in the order to be produced and placed for disposal of the Court when required or to appear and show cause as to why he should not furnish security. The aforesaid provision pre-supposes that upon a prayer to make any order of attachment, there must be a direction to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 either to furnish security or to appear and show cause as to why he should not furnish security and the direction could not be given or communicated unless a notice is issued and served upon the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. 

 "It is clear that before an order of attachment of property before judgment is passed, the Court should issue notice to the opposite party calling upon him to furnish security for satisfying any decree that may eventually be passed against him or to show cause why he should not furnish security and it is only when he had appeared and failed to furnish the security or show cause that the Court can under rule 6 pass an order attaching his property." 

 "The only question which arises in this appeal is whether the lighter age was attachable under Order XXXVIII rule 5 of the Code. Attachment under the rule could be made if there was an attempt on the part of the defendant to remove the vessel from the jurisdiction of the Court with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of the decree. It having been appellants from a foreign country to do a very temporary and specific task of discharge of wheat and that, as such, it could not be attached before judgment, there cannot be any attachment under the rule on the basis of some agreement of the defendant to get the vessel attached. If any right of attachment had accrued in favour of the plaintiff on the basis of such agreement on grounds other than those mentioned in Order XXXVIII rule 5 of the Code; the plaintiff is to take step for necessary relief in an appropriate proceeding but it is not entitled to any relief on an application as framed under Order XXXVIII rule 5 of the Code." 

 15. In the aforesaid premises, the proceeds of the letter of credit do not squarely come within the provision of Order XXXVIII rule 5 for attachment before judgment for which the Court could interfere asking for furnishing security or by attachment before judgment in order to satisfy any possible decree that may be passed in the suit.
